claim: Charter / The pipeline: 'the letterform carries the feeling' — a hand-drawn skeleton carries the source (Nosifer bleeds 'too late', Bangers shouts 'NO'), canny-lock keeps it legible, diffusion supplies the emotional material, and a negative-space knockout can make the void speak louder.

pieces.what: One word walked through the four stages — bare skeleton, canny-locked photoreal, ink stylize, negative-space knockout — step by step, so the reader sees which stage adds the feeling and which keeps the spelling.

The seven BLUELINE voices as a grid (too late, NO, BURNING, THOOM, stay, real, ascension): read each without its caption, then reveal who says it to whom — does the letterform alone tell you the speaker's state?
Same word, mechanical font vs hand-drawn skeleton through the same stylize pass — tests 'mechanical fonts dominate'.
Negative-space variant on a light vs dark energy field — tests 'negative space sings only on a light field'.
